meta.tagline: One of the world's most expensive islands — but this is also where you find the spirit of the Aegean islands in its purest form

pills: Be prepared for July-August crowds or avoid them
Get lost in Chora early in the morning
See Agios Sostis before the beach clubs

overview.intro: Mykonos is like two different islands. The first: some of the world's most expensive beach clubs, mega yachts, nightlife and Paradise Beach packed to bursting in July and August. The second: whitewashed walls, narrow labyrinthine streets, windmills and blue-domed Chora, hidden at the heart of the island. This second Mykonos shows itself in the early morning hours or out of season. The island is small — everything is reachable by vehicle or bus. But before coming to Mykonos, one thing needs to be accepted: everything here is expensive and in midsummer it is very crowded. If you come at peace with that reality, Mykonos won't disappoint.

local_word.definition: Greek for 'town' or 'city' — the main town of every island in the Aegean is called Chora. In Mykonos, Chora is the white labyrinthine heart of the island. Narrow streets, whitewashed walls, blue doors, climbing plants. Deliberately designed like a maze — in the old days to confuse pirates. Today getting lost is just as easy and just as beautiful.

rules.title: If you want to come in July-August, prepare your budget and your patience
rules.description: In midsummer Mykonos fills with crowds from all over the world. Hotel prices are very high, restaurant reservations are essential, finding a spot on the beaches is difficult. June or September offers the same sunshine and sea, prices noticeably lower and crowds at a tolerable level.

rules.title: Explore Chora in the early morning hours
rules.description: During the day Chora's narrow streets get clogged with tourist crowds. But between 7am and 9am the streets are nearly empty — apart from cats and pigeons. At this hour it's possible to take photos, have a quiet coffee and get lost. Beautiful in the evenings too, but the early morning is something else entirely.

rules.title: Hire a vehicle — ideal for discovering the island in a day
rules.description: Mykonos is small but KTEL buses don't go everywhere. Hiring an ATV is the most practical way to reach the island's northern coves, Ano Mera village and hidden beaches. Small car or motorbike are also options. In midsummer, hire in the early morning — by afternoon the good vehicles are gone.

quick_facts.label: Getting there
quick_facts.sub: Flight from Athens ~45 min · fast ferry from Piraeus 2-2.5 hrs · Rafina 1.5-2 hrs

quick_facts.label: On the island
quick_facts.sub: KTEL ticket €1-3 cash · ATV daily €25-50 · taxis expensive and scarce

quick_facts.label: Weather
quick_facts.sub: May–Jun and Sep–Oct ideal · Jul–Aug very crowded · Nov–Mar quiet

quick_facts.label: Food
quick_facts.sub: Street snacks €3-6 · taverna lunch €18-30 · Chora harbourfront very expensive

tip.label: Little Venice — ideal for late afternoon
tip.text: Chora's most iconic corner — colourful houses with balconies and terraces hanging over the sea. Sunset here is spectacular. Busy and expensive at midday. Sitting with a glass of wine between 5pm and 7pm is one of Mykonos's finest moments. Tables fill up quickly — go early.

overview.title: Welcome to Mykonos

transport.intro: Mykonos is a small island. KTEL buses cover the main spots; an ATV or vehicle is essential for the rest.

items.title: From Athens to Mykonos
items.description: Flight from Athens approximately 45 minutes, ticket €40-120 depending on season and how far in advance. Ferry: fast ferry from Piraeus (Seajet, Golden Star) 2-2.5 hours, €50-80. From Rafina port 1.5-2 hours, slightly cheaper. Rafina is close to Athens Airport — KTEL bus 30-40 minutes, €4. Buy tickets in advance in summer — sells out.

items.title: KTEL buses — island transport
items.description: Mykonos has two bus terminals: Fabrika (south) and Old Port (north) — no connection between them but 15 minutes on foot through Chora. From Fabrika: Paradise Beach (~15 min) and the airport (~10 min). From Old Port: the new port and Agios Stefanos. Ticket €1-3, cash from the driver.

items.title: ATV and vehicle hire
items.description: The most free-spirited way to explore the island. ATV daily €25-50, small car €40-70, motorbike €20-40. Essential for reaching the northern coves, Ano Mera village, Fokos and Agios Sostis beaches. Driving licence required. Hire in the early morning — by afternoon the best vehicles are gone. Return with a full tank.

items.title: Boat — beach and island excursions
items.description: Daily boat trips to Delos Island depart from Old Port pier — return approximately €20-25. Combined ticket with Rhenia €25-30. Private boat and catamaran hire also available. Water taxi between beaches: Platis Gialos to Paradise Beach by water taxi 10-15 minutes, €10-15.

items.title: Walking — sufficient within Chora
items.description: Chora's labyrinth is walkable — small and compact. From the windmills to Little Venice 10 minutes, Paraportiani 5 minutes. Getting out of Chora requires KTEL or a vehicle. Coastal walking path and Chora-Ano Mera trail for the more adventurous.

callout.label: Delos Island — 30 minutes from Mykonos, thousands of years back
callout.text: Daily boat trips from Mykonos Old Port. Centre of the ancient Greek pantheon — Temple of Apollo, lion statues, mosaic-floored houses. UNESCO World Heritage Site. Archaeological museum on the island. Return boat ticket plus archaeological site entry combined total €30-35. Take the first morning sailing. Very hot in summer — hat and water essential.

transport.title: Getting Around

stay.intro: Where you stay in Mykonos completely changes the experience — Chora is unmatched but expensive; the south coast is close to beaches but crowded.

local_word.definition: The Aegean summer wind — a strong, constant wind blowing from the north in July and August. In Mykonos the meltemi can blow very powerfully: the sea gets choppy, some coves become unswimmable, umbrellas blow away. But that same wind keeps the island cool even at 35°C. Northern beaches are exposed to the meltemi; southern ones are sheltered. Keep this in mind when choosing a beach.

items.name: Chora — the heart of the island
items.description: Mykonos's white labyrinthine town. Everything within walking distance. Windmills, Little Venice, Paraportiani Church and nightlife. Quiet in the morning hours, crowded in the afternoon. Hotel prices are high but the essence of the Mykonos experience is here.

items.name: Platis Gialos — south coast
items.description: 4 kilometres from Chora, a quiet beach village on the south coast. Connected to the Fabrika bus terminal. Water taxi to Paradise Beach and other beaches. Slightly more affordable than Chora. Suitable for families.

items.name: Ornos — quiet and local
items.description: A quiet small bay on the south coast, next to Platis Gialos. Away from the Paradise Beach crowds. Small waterfront restaurants and cafés. 10 minutes from Chora by car.

items.name: Agios Ioannis — sunset village
items.description: Small village on the south-west coast. Known as the filming location of Shirley Valentine. Stunning sunset views facing Delos Island. Small beach and a few restaurants. 15 minutes from Chora by car. Quiet and authentic.

items.name: Around Ano Mera
items.description: In the centre of the island, the only real village. Panagia Tourliani Monastery, local tavernas and authentic Mykonos life. Far from the beach but close to the northern coves. Half the price of Chora. Car essential.

stay.title: Where to Stay

best_time.intro: Mykonos is a summer island — but the difference in price and crowds between midsummer and shoulder seasons is enormous.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Quietest and most affordable
items.description: April and May are quiet in Mykonos. Most venues aren't yet at full capacity but the weather is lovely and there are no crowds. June is the ideal balance point: temperatures 25-28°C, sea swimmable, venues open but far from the July-August crowds. Prices can drop to half those of midsummer.

callout.label: June — Mykonos's most balanced month
callout.text: Temperatures 25-28°C, warm sea, space on the beaches. A morning walk through Chora's streets is possible without crowds. Restaurants can be found without reservations. Nightlife exists but not at midsummer intensity. The second half of June is ideal — both weather and crowds at their most balanced.

items.subtitle: Spring · Fewer crowds, affordable prices, island in bloom

items.label: Summer
items.name: Most lively but most expensive
items.description: July and August see Mykonos at its most lively but also its most crowded and most expensive. Paradise Beach parties, Little Venice evenings, Cavo Paradiso nightclub — all at their peak during this period. Everything requires booking far in advance. The only window to escape the crowds is in the very early morning hours.

callout.label: Paradise Beach — the party culture and the reality
callout.text: Mykonos's legendary beach. Beach parties during the day, open-air clubs in the evening. In midsummer a beach sunbed costs €30-60 per day. But there's a small free section at the end of the beach too. Super Paradise is more gay-friendly and slightly quieter. KTEL bus to Paradise from Fabrika; walk or water taxi to Super Paradise.

items.subtitle: Summer · Beach parties, mega yachts, crowds, prices at their peak

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Second best time
items.description: September and October are Mykonos's most balanced period. Still 22-26°C, the sea is swimmable. Prices have noticeably dropped. Some nightclubs have closed but the island is still running. Chora in the mornings is genuinely empty and beautiful. The meltemi dies down.

callout.label: September — empty beaches, tavernas without reservations
callout.text: Agios Sostis and Fokos beaches are nearly empty in September. In Chora you can wander around choosing a restaurant — no reservation needed. Delos boat trips are still running. The meltemi settles, northern coves become swimmable. The island is peaceful but not yet closed.

items.subtitle: Autumn · Summer crowds gone, sea still warm, prices dropped

items.label: Winter
items.name: Local Mykonos
items.description: From November to March Mykonos belongs largely to its local residents. Most restaurants, bars and boutiques are closed. Weather 12-16°C and windy. But what remains open is genuinely local and cheap. Chora in the morning hours is quiet and photogenic. For those who choose this period consciously, it means seeing the island's real face.

callout.label: Mykonos in winter — a secret for photographers
callout.text: Between December and February Chora's white streets are nearly empty. The light turns golden with the winter sun. No tourists, plenty of cats. Cafés and tavernas open in winter serve the real Mykonos cuisine. A one-night stay can cost as little as a tenth of midsummer prices.

items.subtitle: Winter · Most venues closed, quiet, real island life

best_time.title: When to Go

monthly_highlights.text: Greek Easter and opening: the island wakes in flowers, hotels freshly open, prices reasonable.
The golden window: warm sea, clubs open but half the crowds — Mykonos's smartest season.
The peak: the world's party is here; book everything ahead, ready the wallet, love the morning hours.
Closing calm: last swims, empty lanes, the sunset unchanged — the island returns to itself.

eat.intro: Mykonos is expensive — but if you go to the wrong place it's even more so. Taverna selection is critical — flee the harbourfront, step into the side streets.

local_word.definition: Greek 'lokma' — hot fried dough balls served with honey and cinnamon. Greece's most beloved street sweet. In Mykonos found in Chora's streets and small shops. Crispy outside, soft inside, with Greek honey and sometimes ice cream on top. €4-6 a portion. Perfect as a street snack while walking or alongside coffee.

items.name: Octopus — sun-dried
items.description: Mykonos's most iconic sight: sun-dried octopus hanging on a taverna balcony. Grilled and served with lemon and olive oil. Seeing octopus hanging on the balcony is a good sign for freshness. Portion at coastal tavernas €12-20.
items.tag: Coastal tavernas · portion €12–20 · look for the one hanging on the balcony

items.name: Tiropita and spanakopita
items.description: Greek cheese pie (tiropita) and spinach pie (spanakopita) — thin filo, fresh cheese or spinach filling, baked in butter. Perfect for breakfast. From bakeries or small pastry shops. €2-3. The bakeries in Chora's back streets are the best — easy to find while walking around.
items.tag: Chora back street bakeries · €2–3 · fresh in the morning

items.name: Souvlaki and gyros
items.description: Greece's fast food but quality versions exist in Mykonos. Souvlaki: grilled lamb or chicken on a skewer, pita, tomato, onion and tzatziki. Gyros: döner-style, thinly sliced meat. Small shops outside Chora's centre charge €5-8. Places on the harbourfront charge double.
items.tag: Chora back streets · €5–8 · avoid the harbourfront

items.name: Loukoumades
items.description: Hot dough balls, Greek honey and cinnamon. A few specialist loukoumades shops in Chora. Plain, chocolate or with ice cream versions. €4-6 a portion. Can be eaten sitting or walking. Morning or evening snack.
items.tag: Shops in Chora's streets · €4–6 · eat them hot

items.name: Fresh fish — at Fokos Taverna
items.description: The fish restaurants on Chora's harbourfront are expensive and inconsistent. For genuinely fresh fish go to Fokos Taverna — on the north coast, next to Fokos beach, not easy to reach but the fish is outstanding. Alternative: local tavernas in Ano Mera are both more affordable and fresher.
items.tag: Fokos Taverna · Ano Mera tavernas · portion €15–25

items.name: Meze platter and Greek wine
items.description: Greek meze sharing culture: tzatziki, tarama, fava (yellow pea purée), stuffed vine leaves, olives, white cheese. A leisurely meal with wine that stretches on. Santorini Assyrtiko is the best match. Glass €8-12, bottle €25-45.
items.tag: Local tavernas · meze platter €12–18 · try Assyrtiko wine

callout.label: Ano Mera — eating at half Chora's price
callout.text: 8 kilometres east of Chora, the island's only real village. Tavernas around the square in front of Panagia Tourliani Monastery are both cheaper and far more local. A menu that costs €30-40 in Chora is €15-20 here. 15-20 minutes by car. Having lunch here and then heading to the northern beaches makes for a perfect day plan.

eat.title: What to Eat

hidden_gems.intro: Mykonos's finest corners are far from the beach clubs — on the north coast, in quiet coves and in the early morning hours.

items.name: Agios Sostis beach
items.description: A small cove on the northern part of the island, reached by vehicle or a long walk. No beach club, no sunbeds, no bar — just sand, rock and clean water. Kiki's Taverna alongside, no reservations and with a queue but both delicious and affordable. Even in midsummer, far from the crowds.
items.rarity: Mykonos beach for those wanting to escape the crowds

items.name: Delos Island
items.description: 30 minutes by boat from Mykonos Old Port. The sacred island of ancient Greece — where Apollo and Artemis are said to have been born. The Terrace of the Lions, mosaic-floored houses, temple ruins. UNESCO World Heritage Site. Take the first morning sailing, bring a hat and water. Closed for visits in winter.
items.rarity: Even older than Delos — the sacred island of the Aegean

items.name: Paraportiani Church
items.description: At the northern end of Chora, on a slope facing the sea. A cumulative white structure made up of five separate chapels. Considered one of the world's most photographed churches. Nearly empty between 7am and 8am. In the afternoon, crowds with cameras at every corner. The church interior is small and plain but the atmosphere is very powerful.
items.rarity: Paraportiani Church — one of the world's most photographed churches

items.name: Fokos beach and Fokos Taverna
items.description: In the north-east of the island, at the end of a steep road reached by vehicle. Completely natural, no facilities. The adjacent Fokos Taverna is known as Mykonos's finest fish restaurant — local produce, fresh fish, no reservations. Quiet even in midsummer. ATV or car essential. Plan a day trip that includes lunch here.
items.rarity: An isolated beach experience in the northerly wind

items.name: Cine Manto
items.description: In the centre of Chora, inside a garden. A tradition much loved in Greece: open-air cinema on summer nights, continuing since the 1960s. Old Hollywood classics and modern films under the pine trees. Watching a film at night with tsipouro (local distilled spirit) and meze is another experience altogether. Ticket €10-12, reservation recommended.
items.rarity: Cine Manto — open-air cinema under the stars

items.name: Ano Mera village
items.description: In the centre of the island, the island's only real inland village. The square around Panagia Tourliani Monastery, local cafés and tavernas. Very different from Mykonos Chora's white labyrinth — simpler, more local, quieter. A small market every day of the week. 15-20 minutes from Chora by car.

callout.label: The windmills — different in the morning and evening
callout.text: The seven 16th-century windmills on the top of Chora are the symbol of Mykonos. Built to mill grain brought by the Aegean winds. Surrounded by photo crowds during the day. Between 7am and 8am in the morning or at sunset in the evening — both light and quiet are at their finest at those hours. The mill interiors are closed but the surroundings can be visited at any time.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Gems

items.label: Get lost in Chora between 7am and 9am
items.sub: Streets empty, light beautiful, ideal for photos. Paraportiani Church and windmills at their finest at this hour.

items.label: Go to Little Venice in the late afternoon
items.sub: Between 5pm and 7pm. A glass of wine, terrace over the sea. Tables fill before sunset — go early.

items.label: Go to Delos Island
items.sub: Boat from Old Port, ~30 min. First morning sailing. Total ~€30-35. Hat and water essential.

items.label: Go to Agios Sostis beach
items.sub: North coast. Car or ATV essential. No beach club. Kiki's Taverna nearby. Go in the early morning.

items.label: Go to Fokos beach and taverna
items.sub: North-east coast. Car essential. Mykonos's finest fresh fish. No reservations — arrive early.

items.label: Visit Paraportiani Church early in the morning
items.sub: North end of Chora. Empty between 7am and 8am. White structure of five chapels. Essential for photos.

items.label: Have lunch in Ano Mera
items.sub: 15-20 min from Chora by car. Local food at half the price. Visit Panagia Tourliani Monastery too.

items.label: Eat loukoumades — hot and with honey
items.sub: Shops in Chora's streets. €4-6. Greek honey and cinnamon. Eat them hot.

items.label: Go to Cine Manto
items.sub: Chora centre, open-air cinema. ~€10-12. Watch a film with tsipouro and meze. Reservation recommended.

items.label: Hire an ATV or vehicle — discover the island in a day
items.sub: Hire in the early morning. Northern coves, Ano Mera, Fokos. ATV daily €25-50.

items.label: Eat octopus — at a taverna with one hanging on the balcony
items.sub: Dry octopus hanging on the balcony means it's fresh. Portion €12-20.

items.label: See the windmills in the morning or at sunset
items.sub: Top of Chora. 7am or sunset. Very crowded at midday.

checklist.title: Mykonos Checklist
checklist.completion_message: You leave Mykonos thinking it's expensive but right — next time you'll come out of season.

traps.title: Skip the Traps
traps.intro: Mykonos is a two-faced island: the bright shop window and the quiet back. Know these four and choose the one without the bill.

items.name: A sunbed at the famous beach clubs
items.description: Front-row sunbeds at the celebrated southern clubs rent for hundreds of euros; two coves over, the sea is the same blue.
items.instead: Turn north: at Agios Sostis and Fokos there are no clubs and no speakers — lay your towel and take the sea for free.

items.name: A 'Greek taverna' with a doorway inviter in Chora
items.description: Most places waving menus in the narrow lanes sell frozen moussaka at view prices.
items.instead: Sit where the locals sit: Ano Mera's square and the backstreet tavernas serve the same dish at half the price with twice the care.

items.name: Counting on taxis
items.description: The island has a handful of taxis; waiting for one after the clubs takes hours and the haggling ends badly.
items.instead: Use the SeaBus between beaches, the bus network is surprisingly good; if you rent wheels, decide who's driving at night before you start.

items.name: The 'sunset table' booking fee in Little Venice
items.description: Some bars charge extra for the window seat; but the sunset belongs to no one.
items.instead: Sit on the wall by the windmills: same sunset, zero fee. If you're drinking anyway, one cocktail's price includes the view.

callout.label: The golden rule
callout.text: On Mykonos the wind (meltemi) picks your beach: north wind means calm southern coves, south wind means quiet northern beaches. Watch the wind, not the sunbeds.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: Chora at dawn, a cove at noon, windmills at dusk

steps.title: Chora — before the crowds
steps.description: Get lost in the white labyrinth: bougainvillea, cats and boutiques not yet open. The best photos happen now.

steps.title: Paraportiani + the old port
steps.description: The white miracle of five churches melted into one; then the fishermen and the heirs of Petros the pelican.

steps.title: Escape to Agios Sostis
steps.description: The sea in the north's untouched cove: no club, no umbrella, pure Aegean.

steps.title: Lunch — a Kiki's-style taverna
steps.description: Grilled octopus, horiatiki, cold white wine; no electricity, no hurry, plenty of flavour.

steps.title: Ano Mera pause
steps.description: A monastery courtyard and a square coffee in the island's inland village; island life, not a tourist window.

steps.title: Sunset at the windmills
steps.description: Sit on the wall before Kato Mili as the sun drops into the Aegean; then a glass in Little Venice and dinner in Chora.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the island as a guest, not a tourist

steps.title: Chora and the northern coves
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: labyrinth at dawn, Agios Sostis at noon, windmills at dusk.

steps.title: Delos morning
steps.description: First boat to the ancient island: walk the Terrace of the Lions where Apollo was born (hat + water mandatory). Rest on a southern beach in the afternoon.

steps.title: The wild east and cinema night
steps.description: Fokos beach and its taverna in the morning (dirt road, worth it), Chora shopping in the afternoon, and a film under the stars in Cine Manto's garden.

phrases.title: The 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Even three words of Greek get the ouzo flowing at the taverna.

items.meaning: Hello / goodbye — the formal, safe greeting
Thank you — looks hard, lands by the second try
Please / you're welcome — Greek's joker card
Cheers! — ouzo glasses rise to this
The exclamation of joy — for breaking plates and starting dances alike
